Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• First-episode sudden left-sided headache (pain 6/10) with blurred “zig-zag” vision, photophobia, nausea and two episodes of vomiting.  
• No focal neurological deficits, gait normal.  
• Family history of migraine.  

Working diagnosis  
• Migraine with aura – unilateral pain, visual aura, nausea/vomiting, photophobia, family history consistent.  

Considerations  
• Subarachnoid hemorrhage – sudden onset “first” headache; rule out if pain worsens or neuro signs develop.  
• Carotid/vertebral artery dissection – unilateral pain with visual disturbance and dizziness; low–medium likelihood.  
• Acute meningitis – low likelihood given absence of fever/neck stiffness but keep in mind if symptoms evolve.  

Management  
• Trial oral ibuprofen plus antiemetic (OTC combination) and oral sugary carbonated drink as first-line acute migraine therapy.  
• Arrange same-day in-person appointment for full neurological examination; patient to attend earlier if deterioration.  
• Advise emergency presentation (ED) if severe worsening, confusion, focal weakness, or persistent vomiting.  
• If symptoms resolve with medication prior to appointment, patient may cancel but to re-contact if recurrence.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Migraine with aura – High likelihood. Unilateral headache, visual zig-zag aura, nausea/vomiting, photophobia, positive family history, no neuro deficit.  
2. Subarachnoid hemorrhage – Medium likelihood. Sudden “first” headache with nausea/vomiting; must be excluded despite moderate pain rating and lack of neuro signs.  
3. Carotid/vertebral artery dissection – Low–Medium likelihood. Unilateral headache with visual disturbance and dizziness; absence of neck pain/trauma lowers probability.
